why does food brown when i fry it but never when i boil it

Browning is the Maillard reaction: at high heat, sugars and amino acids recombine into hundreds of new molecules, which is where roasted smells come from. 🍟 It needs a dry surface and temperatures well above water's boiling point. Boiling pins the food at 100°C and keeps it soaking wet, so the reaction never starts — pale boiled potato, golden fried one, same potato. [CHIPS]What is caramelisation|Why crusts taste better[/CHIPS]

what makes a sentence a run on

A run-on welds two complete sentences together with nothing strong enough between them: I missed the bus I walked. The comma splice is its sibling: I missed the bus, I walked ✍️ You have four repairs — full stop, semicolon, a joining word like so, or a comma plus that word. Length is not the fault; a long sentence can be perfectly built. Repair mine your way.[CHIPS]So I walked|Semicolon version|Long correct example[/CHIPS]

how do cactus plants survive in a desert

They rewrote the usual trade-off. Any plant that opens its pores for carbon dioxide loses water at the same time, so a cactus opens them only in the cool night and stores that carbon as an acid. Next day it makes sugar with the pores clamped shut. 🌵 The fat stem is a water tank, the spines are shrunken leaves, and wide shallow roots grab rain the moment it lands.
[QUIZ]So when does a cactus open its leaf pores?[/QUIZ]
[CHIPS]At night|At noon|Never at all[/CHIPS]

what is gluten and why do people talk about it so much

Gluten is a stretchy network that forms when two wheat proteins, glutenin and gliadin, meet water and get kneaded. why does adding up the digits tell you if a number divides by 9

Because every place value is one more than a run of nines. Take 342, which is 3 hundreds + 4 tens + 2, and notice 100 is 99 + 1 while 10 is 9 + 1. A recording captures only the air path. That thinner, higher voice is the one everyone else has always heard, so it is unfamiliar rather than wrong 🎤.

why is tamil so different from hindi

Because they are not related — not distantly, not at all. 🌏 Tamil belongs to the Dravidian family. Hindi belongs to a completely different family, Indo-European, which also holds Persian, Greek and English; inside that family Hindi sits on the Indo-Aryan branch. That is why Hindi's do and English's two turn out to be cousins, while Tamil's irandu is related to neither. Centuries of living side by side means the two swap words freely — but the skeleton underneath is built differently.

why do websites not store your actual password

Because a stolen database should not hand over your login. Sites store a hash instead: a one-way scramble that is easy to run forwards and impractical to run backwards. When you sign in they hash what you typed and compare scrambles, never the password itself — which is why a real site can reset your password but can never tell you the old one. 🔐 Good sites pick a deliberately slow hash too, so guessing millions of passwords stays expensive. how does a footballer bend a free kick around the wall

Strike across the ball with the inside of the foot and you leave it spinning sideways as it flies. A spinning ball drags air faster round one side than the other, so the pressure difference nudges it off a straight line — physicists call it the Magnus effect. ⚽ The curve grows as the ball slows near the end, which is why the bend looks so sudden. Same physics as a table-tennis topspin dip.

why do people use the median for salaries instead of the mean

why do the monsoon winds change direction twice a year
